points.title: 早年求学
points.description: 山本五十六出生于日本新潟县长冈市，原名高野五十六。其父高野贞吉是地方官员。1893年，山本的父亲因参与政治斗争被暗杀，家庭陷入困境。1901年，山本考入江田岛海军兵学校，开始了他的海军生涯。在校期间，他展现出卓越的才能，特别是在数学和英语方面表现突出。1904年毕业时，他在188名学员中排名第7，成绩优异。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Nagaoka, Niigata Prefecture, Japan, Isoroku Yamamoto was originally named Goro Takano. His father, Sadayoshi Takano, was a local official. In 1893, Yamamoto's father was assassinated due to his involvement in political struggles, plunging the family into hardship. In 1901, Yamamoto entered the Imperial Japanese Naval Academy at Etajima, beginning his naval career. During his studies, he demonstrated exceptional talent, particularly in mathematics and English. Upon graduation in 1904, he ranked 7th out of 188 cadets, showing outstanding academic performance.

points.title: 海军军官生涯
points.description: 山本五十六在日俄战争期间首次参战，担任巡洋舰'日进号'的少尉军官。在1905年的对马海战中，他所在舰艇被鱼雷击中，失去左手食指和中指，这一经历让他深刻认识到现代海战的残酷性。战后，山本赴美国哈佛大学学习，1916年毕业。这段经历使他成为日本海军中少数了解美国文化的军官。1923年，山本晋升为海军少佐，1928年担任'赤城号'航空母舰舰长，开始重视海军航空兵的发展。
points.descriptionEn: During the Russo-Japanese War, Yamamoto first saw combat as an ensign on the cruiser Nisshin. In the Battle of Tsushima in 1905, his ship was torpedoed, resulting in the loss of his index and middle fingers on his left hand. This experience gave him a profound understanding of the brutality of modern naval warfare. After the war, Yamamoto studied at Harvard University, graduating in 1916. This experience made him one of the few Japanese naval officers with an understanding of American culture. In 1923, he was promoted to commander, and in 1928, he became captain of the aircraft carrier Akagi, beginning his emphasis on naval aviation development.

points.title: 外交使命
points.description: 1929年，山本五十六被派往美国担任海军武官，常驻华盛顿。在美国期间，他广泛考察了美国的工业实力、军事技术和民众生活，对美国强大的工业基础和军事潜力印象深刻。他多次向日本海军高层报告美国的强大实力，警告不要与美国开战。这段经历使山本成为日本海军中少有的对美强硬派持谨慎态度的将领。1930年，山本参与伦敦海军裁军会议，代表日本谈判。1934年，他返回日本，晋升为海军少将。
points.descriptionEn: In 1929, Yamamoto was assigned to the United States as a naval attaché, stationed in Washington. During his time in America, he extensively studied the country's industrial strength, military technology, and civilian life, becoming deeply impressed with America's robust industrial base and military potential. He repeatedly reported to Japanese naval leadership about America's strength, warning against war with the United States. This experience made Yamamoto one of the few Japanese naval officers who maintained a cautious attitude toward confronting America. In 1930, he participated in the London Naval Conference, representing Japan in negotiations. In 1934, he returned to Japan and was promoted to rear admiral.

points.title: 航空战略家
points.description: 1936年，山本五十六担任海军航空本部技术部长，开始大力推动日本海军航空兵的发展。他认识到航空力量在未来海战中的决定性作用，主张建立强大的航空舰队。山本亲自参与设计了多种舰载飞机，并推动航空母舰的现代化改造。他支持开发零式战斗机等先进机型，这些飞机在太平洋战争初期发挥了重要作用。1939年，山本晋升为海军中将，并担任第一舰队司令长官，进一步实践他的海空一体作战理念。
points.descriptionEn: In 1936, Yamamoto became head of the Technical Bureau of the Naval Aviation Department, vigorously promoting the development of Japanese naval aviation. He recognized the decisive role of air power in future naval warfare and advocated for the establishment of a powerful aviation fleet. Yamamoto personally participated in designing various carrier-based aircraft and promoted the modernization of aircraft carriers. He supported the development of advanced aircraft like the Zero fighter, which played a crucial role in the early stages of the Pacific War. In 1939, Yamamoto was promoted to vice admiral and became commander-in-chief of the First Fleet, further implementing his naval-air integrated warfare concept.

points.title: 联合舰队司令
points.description: 1940年，山本五十六晋升为海军大将，并被任命为联合舰队司令长官。他策划并指挥了1941年的珍珠港袭击，这一行动重创了美国太平洋舰队。随后，山本指挥了日本在太平洋战争初期的胜利，包括马来亚海战和爪哇海战等。然而，随着战争形势变化，山本对日本的战争前景日益悲观。他反对与美国开战，但作为军人，他必须执行命令。1943年4月18日，山本的座机在布干维尔岛上空被美国战斗机拦截并击落，山本五十六当场身亡，终年58岁。
points.descriptionEn: In 1940, Yamamoto was promoted to admiral and appointed commander-in-chief of the Combined Fleet. He planned and commanded the 1941 Pearl Harbor attack, which dealt a heavy blow to the US Pacific Fleet. Subsequently, Yamamoto directed Japan's early victories in the Pacific War, including the Battle of Malaya and the Battle of the Java Sea. However, as the war situation changed, Yamamoto became increasingly pessimistic about Japan's prospects. He opposed war with the United States but, as a military officer, had to follow orders. On April 18, 1943, Yamamoto's plane was intercepted and shot down by American fighters over Bougainville Island, resulting in his death at the age of 58.

points.title: 国葬与遗产
points.description: 山本五十六死后，日本政府为他举行了盛大的国葬，他在日本被视为民族英雄。然而，随着日本战败，他的评价变得复杂。山本被塑造成一个悲剧英雄形象，一个反对战争却不得不执行命令的军人。他的军事才能得到认可，特别是对海军航空兵发展的贡献。在流行文化中，山本的形象经常被描绘为一位具有西方思维、了解美国实力的日本将领，这种形象既反映了他真实的经历，也带有一定的神话色彩。
points.descriptionEn: After Yamamoto's death, the Japanese government held a grand state funeral for him, and he was regarded as a national hero in Japan. However, with Japan's defeat, his evaluation became more complex. Yamamoto was portrayed as a tragic hero—a military officer who opposed war but had to follow orders. His military talent was recognized, particularly his contributions to the development of naval aviation. In popular culture, Yamamoto is often depicted as a Japanese commander with Western thinking and an understanding of American strength, an image that reflects both his actual experiences and certain mythological elements.

supporter.zh: 山本五十六被视为日本海军的传奇人物和战略天才。他敏锐地认识到航空力量在现代海战中的决定性作用，大力推动日本海军航空兵的发展，为日本在太平洋战争初期的胜利奠定了基础。作为联合舰队司令，他策划的珍珠港袭击展现了卓越的军事才能和冒险精神。山本对美国的了解使他成为日本军方中少有的对美开战持谨慎态度的将领，这种战略远见值得肯定。他的悲剧性结局更增添了英雄色彩，被视为一位为国捐躯的忠诚军人。
supporter.en: Yamamoto is regarded as a legendary figure and strategic genius of the Japanese Navy. He keenly recognized the decisive role of air power in modern naval warfare, vigorously promoting the development of Japanese naval aviation, which laid the foundation for Japan's early victories in the Pacific War. As commander of the Combined Fleet, the Pearl Harbor attack he planned demonstrated exceptional military talent and adventurous spirit. Yamamoto's understanding of America made him one of the few Japanese military leaders who cautiously opposed war with the United States, a strategic foresight worthy of recognition. His tragic death added to his heroic image, seen as a loyal soldier who sacrificed his life for his country.

critic.zh: 批评者认为山本五十六作为珍珠港袭击的主要策划者，应对太平洋战争的爆发负重要责任。尽管他个人对与美国开战持保留态度，但作为日本海军高级将领，他仍然执行了侵略政策，导致大量人员伤亡。他的军事决策虽然战术上成功，但战略上短视，未能预见美国强大的工业潜力将最终决定战争走向。此外，山本对日本军国主义的扩张政策虽有疑虑却未采取有效抵制，被视为体制内的妥协者，而非真正的和平主义者。
critic.en: Critics argue that as the main planner of the Pearl Harbor attack, Yamamoto bears significant responsibility for the outbreak of the Pacific War. Despite his personal reservations about going to war with America, as a senior Japanese naval officer, he still implemented aggressive policies that led to numerous casualties. His military decisions, though tactically successful, were strategically shortsighted, failing to anticipate America's industrial potential that would ultimately determine the war's outcome. Furthermore, although Yamamoto had doubts about Japanese militarist expansion policies, he did not effectively resist them, seen as a compromiser within the system rather than a true pacifist.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，山本五十六被复杂地塑造为一个矛盾的人物。他既是日本军国主义的执行者，又是对西方文化有深入了解的现代化海军将领。历史学者普遍认可他对海军航空兵发展的贡献，同时批评他参与侵略战争的行为。在流行文化中，山本经常被描绘为一位具有悲剧色彩的军事天才，一个了解美国实力却不得不执行命令的矛盾人物。这种多元评价反映了历史人物的多面性，也体现了人们对战争与和平、忠诚与良知等永恒主题的思考。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Yamamoto is portrayed as a complex and contradictory figure. He was both an executor of Japanese militarism and a modern naval commander with deep understanding of Western culture. Historians generally acknowledge his contributions to naval aviation development while criticizing his involvement in aggressive warfare. In popular culture, Yamamoto is often depicted as a tragic military genius—a contradictory figure who understood American strength but had to follow orders. This multifaceted evaluation reflects the complexity of historical figures and embodies people's contemplation of eternal themes like war and peace, loyalty and conscience.

self.zh: 如果战争持续一年以上，我毫无信心能取得胜利。
self.en: If war goes on for more than a year, I have no confidence of victory.

others.zh: 山本五十六是一位卓越的海军战略家，他理解现代海战的本质，但不幸的是，他为错误的事业服务。
others.en: Isoroku Yamamoto was an outstanding naval strategist who understood the nature of modern naval warfare, but unfortunately, he served the wrong cause.
